text:
eden: hitting a weird one. running local-serve inside a k8s pod that mounts devs' home via NFS. redwoodctl can't write profiles.json and local-serve fails with \"profiles store not writable\".

sam: NFS uid/gid mismatch? what does `ls -l ~/.redwood` show inside the pod?

eden: shows owner uid 1001 but pod runs as 1000. tried chmod 777 as a stopgap but that broke concurrent lock semantics and caused racey errors.

kaya: we had a similar case: NFS-mounted home + locking using file-based locks = brittle. locking on NFS sometimes doesn't work across clients (flock vs lockf). which lock method does redwoodctl use?

eden: looks like file lock + pid file under $CONFIG_DIR/profiles.lock. error log: \"failed to acquire lock: operation not supported on transport\".

nfs-bot: FYI NFSv4 doesn't support POSIX advisory locks reliably when mount uses noac or certain export options. Recommend using a shared DB/kv for locks or per-node local lock fallback.

sam: temporary fixes: 1) run redwoodctl with `--config-dir /tmp/redwood-config` so locks are local to the pod 2) set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/redwood-config before invoking local-serve.

ekden: workaround worked. but uncovered another issue: when I switched config-dir, redwoodctl login had cached token in the old store and local-serve spawned `redwoodctl login` which opened device flow that printed URL to the pod stdout (ugly) but didn't surface back to the developer. we need better handling for non-interactive spawned logins.

kaya: agree. local-serve should accept `--config-dir` and pass it when it spawns redwoodctl. also it should detect non-tty and print the device code in the parent logs, not hide it in child stdout.

sam: also consider a per-pod ephemeral token mode for localtests: `local-serve --token-file /run/secrets/redwood-token` or `--token-env REDWOOD_API_KEY`. avoids spawning login at all for ephemeral CI/dev pods.

eden: that would be ideal. in CI we already inject a token env. but for interactive dev pods we rely on login. still, passing env through spawn would help.

kaya: small doc change: add an NFS note under "Troubleshooting: config dir and mounts". example snippet we used:

```
# Pod manifest snippet: make config dir local to container
volumeMounts:
  - name: tmp-redwood
    mountPath: /tmp/redwood-config
volumes:
  - name: tmp-redwood
    emptyDir: {}
env:
  - name: REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR
    value: /tmp/redwood-config
```

sam: another edge: when profiles.json is present on NFS but unreadable due to root_squash, redwoodctl attempts to migrate profiles and creates a backup under /ProgramData style path which isn't mounted here and fails. we should make migration fail softer and print one-liner remediation.

eden: error I saw: \"migration failed: cannot write backup: permission denied\" and local-serve crashed. a softer behavior would be: log migration failure + continue in read-only mode or prompt to set config-dir.

kaya: filed PDE-734: make config migrate non-fatal and add a `--migrate-only` flag so ops can run migration as a separate safe step.

devex-bot: PDE-734 created: make config migrate non-fatal; add --migrate-only and improve spawned-login logging.

sam: one more subtle auth thing: when redwoodctl is installed via distro package, some distros package it under /usr/bin/redwoodctl and create a systemd-auth helper that uses a different HOME. spawn path confusion causes token lookup misses. local-serve should prefer explicit config-dir over relying on PATH-installed defaults.

ekden: agreed. for now i'm adding a short checklist to our onboarding doc: 
- set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR if using NFS or containerized dev 
- prefer ephemeral /tmp config for pod-local runs 
- set REDWOODCTL_SKIP_AUTOLOGIN=1 during global installs in CI and run `redwoodctl login --token` as a separate step

kaya: nice. also add an example `local-serve --token-env REDWOOD_API_KEY` snippet to quickstart so folks running in pods can avoid interactive auth.

sam: i'll pick up PDE-734 and add the `--token-env` option to local-serve and ensure spawn passes config-dir/env. adding tests for NFS mount + no-lock fallback in our infra matrix.

devex-bot: PR opened: eng-platform/pde-734-ephemeral-config-token-env. CI job added to run NFS-mount e2e in a containerized harness.

ekden: thanks everyone. this unblocked dev pods. i'll update the internal doc and share the mount snippet in the quickstart PR. closing after PR merges. :white_check_mark:
